risks.title: Cyber Ransomware Incident
risks.score_rationale: Incident documented explicitly in Item 1A. April 2023 ransomware attack caused data center outage impacting Aloha cloud-based services and Counterpoint. Cumulative costs of $47M incurred with $37M recovered through insurance. Recent and material financial impact.

risks.title: Decline in Product Revenue (Hardware and Software Licenses)
risks.score_rationale: All other revenue (non-recurring) declined 15% in 2025 and 23% in 2024, reflecting the strategic decline of legacy hardware and license-based revenue streams as the company transitions to SaaS and recurring revenue models.

risks.title: Concentration Risk on Recurring Revenue
risks.score_rationale: Recurring revenue increased from 50.9% in 2023 to 62.4% in 2025, while all other revenue contracted from 49.1% to 37.6%. This structural shift increases exposure to disruptions in recurring revenue streams and customer retention.

risks.title: Transformation and Restructuring Costs
risks.score_rationale: Material transformation and restructuring costs are explicitly mentioned as EBITDA adjustments and items affecting results. These represent significant near-term financial burdens as the company executes its strategic transformation to SaaS and platform-based models.

risks.title: Foreign Currency Exposure
risks.score_rationale: The company operates globally with exposure to multiple currencies. Historical impacts from foreign currency devaluation are reflected in EBITDA adjustments, indicating structural exposure to exchange rate fluctuations, particularly in developing markets.

risks.title: Regulatory Compliance and Payment Processing Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company's payments business is subject to complex regulatory requirements from payment networks, card brands, and financial regulations. Non-compliance could result in fines, penalties, revocation of registration, or loss of sponsor bank relationships, any of which could materially harm operations.

ai_positioning.summary: NCR Voyix mentions artificial intelligence in the context of macroeconomic trends and customer demands. The company notes that global shortages of microchips are partially driven by AI adoption. However, no specific AI developments or products are detailed in the 10-K filing.
evidence: Global shortages of microchips and other technology components, primarily driven by the adoption of artificial intelligence
